package: TSOT26 (6-lead, 0.95 mm pitch; ordering code WU = TSOT26)
description: Diodes Inc AP63203Q: automotive-compliant (AEC-Q100 grade 1), 3.8-32 V input, 2 A synchronous buck converter, FIXED 3.3 V output, 1100 kHz switching, PFM/PWM with Frequency Spread Spectrum (+/-6% jitter) and low-dropout (~100% duty) mode. Integrated 125 mOhm high-side / 68 mOhm low-side MOSFETs and internal loop compensation; no external compensation or feedback divider. Key electricals: VFB (= VOUT) 3.267/3.300/3.333 V CCM; fSW 990/1100/1210 kHz CCM; built-in soft-start tSS = 4 ms typ; HS peak current limit 2.35/2.8/3.25 A; LS valley limit 3.2 A typ; IQ 22 uA typ (no-load, non-switching); ISHDN 1 uA; VIN POR rising 3.5/3.7 V max, UVLO falling 3.06 V typ; tON_MIN 80 ns; TSD +160 C (recovery +135 C). Protections: UVLO, output OVP (FB > 110% of internal 0.8 V ref), cycle-by-cycle peak current limit with hiccup after 512 cycles / 8192 cycles off, thermal shutdown. Source: Diodes Incorporated DS43698 Rev. 1-2, September 2021 (AP63200Q/AP63201Q/AP63203Q/AP63205Q), 30 pages.

pinout.name: FB
pinout.notes: Feedback sensing terminal for the output voltage. On the FIXED-output AP63203Q the FB pin is tied DIRECTLY to VOUT - 'tie the FB pin directly to VOUT as there is no need for R1, R2, or C4' [Layout note 5, p.27; Figure 4, p.3]. Regulated feedback voltage AP63203Q CCM = 3.267/3.300/3.333 V (min/typ/max) [Electrical Characteristics, p.6]. Internally compared against the 0.8 V reference through an internal divider; OVP trips when FB exceeds 110% of the 0.8 V reference [Sec 6, p.23]. Generic pin table text 'Connect this pin to the resistive divider of the output' applies to the adjustable AP63200Q/AP63201Q [Pin Descriptions, p.4]

pinout.name: EN
pinout.notes: Enable input, digital, high-voltage tolerant (abs max 35 V). Drive high to turn on, low to turn off. 'Connect to VIN or leave floating for automatic startup' [Pin Descriptions, p.4]. An internal 1.5 uA pull-up current source from the internal LDO-regulated VCC to EN guarantees the device still auto-enables if EN is left floating [Sec 3, p.21] - so FLOAT-TO-ENABLE is valid. Precision thresholds: VEN_H 1.18 V typ / 1.25 V max (rising), VEN_L 1.03 V min / 1.09 V typ (falling); IEN 5.5 uA at VEN = 1.5 V, 1.0/1.5/2.0 uA at VEN = 1 V [Electrical Characteristics, p.6]. A 4 uA hysteresis pull-up plus an external R3/R4 divider from VIN sets a higher VIN UVLO (Eq. 2/3, VON > 3.7 V, VOFF > 3.26 V) [Sec 5, p.22-23]. Optional EN-to-GND ceramic capacitor delays startup: Cd[nF] ~ 1.27 * td[ms] (Eq. 1) [Sec 3, p.21]

pinout.name: VIN
pinout.notes: Power input; supplies the IC and the step-down converter power MOSFETs. Drive with a 3.8 V to 32 V source. 'Bypass VIN to GND with a suitably large capacitor to eliminate noise due to the switching of the IC' [Pin Descriptions, p.4]

pinout.name: GND
pinout.notes: Power ground [Pin Descriptions, p.4]. Only ground/thermal terminal on the package - heat leaves the die through this pin and the GND copper (no exposed pad); layout notes 7/8 call for as many vias as possible around GND (and VIN) [p.27]

pinout.name: SW
pinout.notes: Power switching output. 'SW is the switching node that supplies power to the output. Connect the output LC filter from SW to the output load' [Pin Descriptions, p.4]. Hot switching node: place the inductor as close to SW as possible [Layout note 3]. Proprietary multi-level gate driver gives a ringing-free SW node; on the fixed-output AP63203Q/AP63205Q SW resonance ringing is also removed in PFM at 0 A inductor current [Sec 4, p.22]. Abs max -0.3 to VIN+0.3 V DC, -2.5 to VIN+2.0 V for 20 ns

pinout.name: BST
pinout.notes: High-side gate drive boost input. 'A 100nF capacitor is recommended from BST to SW to power the high-side driver' [Pin Descriptions, p.4]; a ceramic capacitor MUST be connected between BST and SW for proper operation [Sec 14, p.26]. Boot UVP: if the bootstrap capacitor falls below 2.3 V the low-side FET is turned on for 220 ns to refresh it back above 2.85 V. Abs max VSW-0.3 to VSW+6.0 V

decoupling.placement: Place the input capacitors as closely across VIN (pin 3) and GND (pin 4) as possible [Layout note 2, p.27]. Figure 77 places C1 directly bridging the VIN and GND copper at the IC pins
decoupling.notes: Input capacitor: 'Using a ceramic capacitor of 10uF or greater is sufficient for most applications'. Low ESR required (ceramic or low-ESR electrolytic) because of the large dI/dt; a tantalum must be surge protected. Select an RMS current rating greater than half the maximum load current [Sec 12, p.26]. Table 2 (AP63203Q, 3.3 V) lists C1 = 10 uF [p.25]

decoupling.placement: Ceramic capacitor connected between the BST (pin 6) and SW (pin 5) pins; Figure 77 puts C3 immediately beside the IC bridging the BST pad to the SW copper [p.27]
decoupling.notes: Bootstrap capacitor for the high-side gate driver: '100nF ceramic capacitor is sufficient'; required for proper operation [Pin Descriptions p.4; Sec 14, p.26]. Table 2 (AP63203Q) C3 = 100 nF [p.25]

pins: VOUT node (inductor output; FB pin 1 ties directly to it on the fixed 3.3 V AP63203Q)
decoupling.placement: Place the output capacitors as close to GND as possible [Layout note 4, p.27]; Figure 77 places C2 bridging the VOUT and GND copper next to the inductor
decoupling.notes: Output capacitor: 'For most applications, a total capacitance of 2 x 22uF using ceramic capacitors is sufficient' [Sec 13, p.26]. Table 2 (AP63203Q, VOUT 3.3 V) C2 = 2 x 22 uF [p.25]. Only a LOWER bound is specified, via Eq. 10: COUT > max(L*ITrans^2/(dVovershoot*VOUT), L*ITrans^2/(dVundershoot*(VIN-VOUT))). Ripple from Eq. 9: VOUT_ripple = dIL*(ESR + 1/(8*fsw*COUT)). No min/max effective-capacitance stability window is published

land_pattern.notes: From 'Suggested Pad Layout', TSOT26, p.29: C = 0.950 (pad pitch within a row), X = 0.700 (pad width), Y = 1.000 (pad length), Y1 = 3.200 (overall tip-to-tip span across both rows). row_spacing_mm = Y1 - Y = 2.200 mm center-to-center is DERIVED from those two printed values (the datasheet prints only the 3.200 tip-to-tip dimension). Package outline (p.29, all mm): A 1.00 max, A1 0.010-0.100, A2 0.840-0.900, D 2.800-3.000 (2.900 typ), E 2.800 BSC, E1 1.500-1.700 (1.600 typ), b 0.300-0.450, c 0.120-0.200, e 0.950 BSC, e1 1.900 BSC, L 0.30-0.50, L2 0.250 BSC. Top view: pin 1 top-left, pins 1-2-3 down the left side (FB, EN, VIN), pins 4-5-6 up the right side (GND, SW, BST). No exposed/thermal pad. Datasheet names the package 'TSOT26' only (ordering code WU); it never uses the name TSOT-23-6. Mechanical: MSL 1 per J-STD-020, matte tin plated leads, 0.013 g

layout_notes: Heat dissipation is a major layout concern at 2 A load; 2 oz copper on both top and bottom layers is recommended [PCB Layout 1, p.27]
Hot loop: place the input capacitors as closely across VIN and GND as possible [PCB Layout 2]
SW node: place the inductor as close to SW as possible; keep the SW copper small [PCB Layout 3; Figure 77]
Place the output capacitors as close to GND as possible [PCB Layout 4]

FB routing: place feedback components as close to FB as possible, if applicable. If using AP63203Q/AP63205Q, tie the FB pin directly to VOUT - there is no need for R1, R2 or C4 [PCB Layout 5]. Figure 77 runs the FB sense as a thin trace from the far (load) side of the inductor back to the FB pin, away from the SW copper
If using four or more layers, use at least the 2nd and 3rd layers as GND to maximize thermal performance [PCB Layout 6]
Add as many vias as possible around the GND pin and under the GND plane for heat dissipation to all GND layers [PCB Layout 7]
Add as many vias as possible around the VIN pin and under the VIN plane for heat dissipation to all VIN layers [PCB Layout 8]

Figure 77 (Recommended PCB Layout, p.27) uses five copper regions: VIN (with C1 across to GND), a large central GND pour peppered with vias, a compact SW pour under the inductor, VOUT (with C2 back to GND), and a small FB island; C3 sits at the IC bridging BST to the SW pour

Theta-JA 89 C/W is specified with the device on FR-4, SINGLE-LAYER PCB, 2 oz copper, with the minimum recommended pad layout [Thermal Resistance note 6, p.5]; TJ must stay below the +150 C maximum recommended operating junction temperature (TRISE = PD * theta-JA, TJ = TA + TRISE, Eq. 4/5, p.23-24)

abs_max.param: VIN supply pin voltage (400 ms transient)
